title: Account Holds on Patient Invoices & Statements
content:
A Patient Invoices & Statements invoice is put on hold for exactly one cause at a time, and statements stop while it is on hold. The questions below are answered from the hold rule.

**What can put an invoice on hold?**
Three causes, recorded on the invoice as its hold reason:

| Hold reason | When it applies |
|---|---|
| Billing dispute | When the patient files a billing dispute on the invoice |
| Assistance review | While a financial-assistance application covering the invoice is pending, and only where the invoice's billing class can receive a financial-assistance discount |
| Insurance reprocessing | While a claim for the invoice's order is corrected, appealed or reprocessed |

**Can one hold carry two causes?**
No. A hold has exactly one cause.

**How long does a hold last?**
According to its cause, in calendar days: a billing-dispute hold lasts the class's billing-dispute hold days, an assistance-review hold the class's financial-assistance review hold days, and an insurance-reprocessing hold the class's insurance-reprocessing hold days. The date the hold started is recorded on the invoice.

**Can a hold be extended?**
Yes, at most the billing class's maximum number of extensions, each extension adding one more period of the same length as the hold.

**When does a hold end?**
A hold is released when its cause is decided, or when it reaches its limit, whichever comes first.

**What happens to the invoice when the hold ends?**

| Balance when the hold is resolved | Result |
|---|---|
| A balance is still due | The invoice returns to open and statements resume |
| The balance is zero | The invoice closes |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A hold whose cause carries a length of 45 calendar days, on a class that permits one extension, can last 45 days, or 90 days in total once extended; it ends earlier on the day its cause is decided. If the cause is decided with adjustments that bring the balance to zero, the invoice closes; if 60.00 is still due, the invoice is open again with 60.00 due and its statements resume.
